newsitem.title: ECUADOR: France criticizes Ecuador on investment rules.
newsitem.headline: France criticizes Ecuador on investment rules.

text.p: France added its voice Monday to diplomatic complaints about the lack of legal protection Ecuador offers foreign investors, with its outgoing ambassador calling it "a country that does not respect agreements."

"There is a tendency here at times for each government to reject international deals made by its predecessor," French envoy Laurent Rapin told reporters. "This is no way to behave, you have to respect international accords."

Rapin, who is being replaced in a few weeks, announced that French President Jacques Chirac would pay an official visit to Ecuador in December 1998. But he also became the latest ambassador to criticize the lack of legal protection for investors in Ecuador, echoing similar comments by British envoy Richard Lavers and U.S. envoy Leslie Alexander.
"Businessmen from my country need very clear and sure rules," said Rapin. "If it changes every year it becomes a very negative issue for investors."
Specifically, he complained that an educational accord with France signed in 1992 was cancelled by a new government a year later.
Earlier this year, France declined to take part in the privatization of 35 percent of Ecuador's state telephone company without explanation, despite initially showing an interest.

Foreign investment has suffered since the election last year of populist Abdala Bucaram. He was ousted by Congress earlier this year following massive popular protests. (( -- Maria Veronica Barreiros, Quito Newsroom, 5932 258429))
